description: Baseline: SCP (credit index / tranche derivatives, illiquid) marked at dealer-quote midpoints through end 2011. Portfolio had generated ~2.0bn gains 2007-2011.
New CIO VaR model becomes effective; SCP VaR falls ~44% to ~57m. Approved while the portfolio was breaching limits.
source: PSI hearing exhibit 77 (OCC emails: 'cio var change effective 1/27/12, VaR -44% to $57mm')

description: Informal change of marking practice: traders stop using midpoints (used until January) and begin marking at the favourable end of the bid-offer spread. No formal methodology change, no committee approval.
source: PSI hearing record (Levin opening: 'stopped using the midpoint prices that they had used up until January'); SEC PR 2013-154 dates concealment to March 2012 - use Jan-Mar as the drift window

description: SCP loses ~69m in January and ~169m in February internally; five major risk limits breached during Q1; limits raised rather than positions cut.
graph_pattern: (pos)-[:GENERATED_SIGNAL]->(s:PnLSignal{unexplained:true}); (pos)-[:SUBJECT_TO_CONTROL]->(c:Control{kind:'risk limit',breached:true}) followed by limit increase instead of Escalation
source: PSI report findings (4) Disregarded Risk; monthly loss figures per report ch. III

description: Internal spreadsheet: YTD reported losses 161m; at midpoint prices losses would be 593m (gap 432m). Document exists, is not escalated; CIO head learns of it only in July.
source: PSI report ch. IV 'Hiding Losses' ('by March 16, 2012 ... $161 million ... $432 million ... $593 million')

description: Daily marks entered at the aggressive end of dealer quotes; desk head at times gives a 'desired daily loss' target. Represent as a series of PriceOverride nodes Jan-Mar (one per business day or per week).
graph_pattern: (pos)-[:OVERRIDDEN_BY]->(po:PriceOverride{deviation_bps, side:'favourable'}) x N; (po)-[:APPROVED_BY]->(a:Approval)-[:APPROVED_BY]->(p:Person{role:'Desk head'}) same desk as pos; NO IPV challenge
source: SEC PR 2013-154 ('marked at the most aggressive end of the dealers' bid-offer spread'; 'desired daily loss target')

description: Trader estimates in email ~600m loss at midpoint / ~300m at 'best' prices; the book reports a 12m daily loss. Same day the CIO head orders traders to stop trading.
source: PSI report ch. IV ('On March 23, Mr. Iksil estimated ... $600 million ... $300 million ... daily loss of only $12 million'; 'on March 23, 2012, CIO head Ina Drew ordered the SCP traders to stop trading')

description: Quarter-end: CIO reports a 319m daily loss. Valuation Control Group review finds a 512m difference between midpoint and used prices at 31 March - and upholds the marks as within tolerance. This is the 'control happened and stopped nothing' scene.
source: PSI report ch. IV ('difference ... between using midpoint prices versus more favorable prices totaled $512 million'; findings (3): reviews 'upheld the suspect values')

description: External trigger: press reports on the 'London Whale' positions. Internal escalation is reactive, not control-driven.
source: PSI report ch. I (media reports April 6, 2012); public record

description: Daily P&L first reported as -6m; 90 minutes later, after a confrontation between two traders, re-issued at roughly -400m.
source: PSI report ch. IV ('On April 10, 2012, the CIO initially reported an estimated daily loss of $6 million, but 90 minutes later ... issued a new P&L report')

description: Public statements minimising the issue ('tempest in a teapot') on the Q1 earnings call. Not a control event; useful as the 'misinformed' marker in the chronology.
source: PSI hearing exhibit 1f 'Inaccurate Public Statements on April 13, 2012'

description: Counterparties dispute the CIO's values; collateral disputes peak at ~690m. External confirmation that marks are off-market.
source: PSI report ch. IV ('collateral disputes peaking at $690 million')

description: Bank announces ~2bn loss on the SCP. Same day the Controller closes a special review concluding the CIO pricing practices were 'consistent with industry practices'.
source: PSI report ch. IV; hearing record (Levin opening)

description: Deputy CRO directs the CIO to mark like the Investment Bank: independent pricing service midpoints. Resolves collateral disputes in counterparties' favour and ends the mismarking.
source: PSI report ch. IV ('In May, the bank's Deputy Chief Risk Officer ... directed the CIO to mark its books in the same manner as the Investment Bank')

description: Synthetic credit portfolio transferred from CIO to the Investment Bank.
source: JPM 8-K/10-Q 2012 ('transfer of the synthetic credit portfolio to the CIB on July 2, 2012')

description: Management internal review concludes traders may not have marked in good faith (recorded calls); Q1 2012 pre-tax income overstated by 660m; restatement announced (filed 9 Aug 2012). Root causes: ineffective CIO governance and risk management, insufficiently granular limits, inadequate VaR model approval.
source: JPM 10-Q Q2/Q3 2012; 10-K 2012 ('On August 9, 2012, the Firm restated'); SEC PR 2013-154 ('overstated by $660 million')

description: Management Task Force report and independent Board review published; OCC issues Cease and Desist order requiring corrective actions.

Senate PSI 300-page report and hearing: findings incl. 'Hid Massive Losses' (>660m), 'Disregarded Risk' (all five major limits breached), recommendation to quantify and investigate deviations from midpoint prices over a month.
SEC charges two former CIO traders with fraudulent mismarking; parallel criminal charges by US Attorney SDNY. Industry-wide regulatory attention to valuation practices follows.
